This is necessary because C# must make all of its decisions around lifetime safety based on the information available in the signature of the method and the lifetime of the values at the call site. When there are `ref` parameters that are `ref struct` then there is the potential that they could swap around their contents. Hence at the call site we must ensure all of these **potential** swaps are compatible. If the language didn't enforce that then it will allow for bad code like the following.
